properties.externalDependency: Historical main.bicep interface only: reviewed external egress/access. The versioned primary bootstrap uses its own Firewall/VPN/route tables/operator without a parallel NVA; it does not invent an existing hub or silently adopt resources.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security: isolate ingress, workloads and private endpoints. Dedicated Flex subnets must not share the Container Apps environment subnet.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The approved platform egress/access connection is a mandatory external gate, not an invented existing resource. CIDRs are examples, not an approved IP allocation.

properties.privateEndpoints: Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints@2024-07-01 with privateDnsZoneGroups@2024-07-01; one endpoint per storage subresource, per PaaS target and for AMPLS.
properties.existingDnsGate: Do not create duplicate zones in a connected landing zone; adapt to existing authoritative zones before deployment.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security/reliability: service FQDNs must resolve privately; AMPLS uses one scope per shared DNS context.
reasoning.tradeoffs: DNS links alone do not provide VPN/peering or conditional forwarding for remote clients.

properties.entraGate: Tenant app registrations, app roles, product grants, user separation and CI federation are separate bootstrap actions, not ARM role assignments.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security: separate deployable identities and no workload credentials. Agent identity has no SQL, evidence-write, approval or transmission privilege.
alternativesConsidered: One privileged identity for every host
reasoning.tradeoffs: Application roles and Azure resource RBAC are distinct; neither substitutes for SQL contained users.

reasoning.whyChosen: Operational excellence: isolated telemetry with explicit short pilot retention.
alternativesConsidered: Using business evidence as operational logs
reasoning.tradeoffs: No daily ingestion hard cap that silently drops watchdog telemetry; cost alerts and reviewed retention are required.

properties.diagnostics: Allowlisted metadata/system logs and metrics only; no model prompts, clinical bodies, SQL batches or search query text.

reasoning.whyChosen: Operational excellence/security: correlate failures without copying medical content into telemetry.
reasoning.tradeoffs: SDK/host redaction and unsampled successful-heartbeat emission require application verification.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security: private application telemetry ingestion and private operator queries.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Diagnostic-setting traffic uses a Microsoft service channel; AMPLS is not a universal outbound filter. Global here is control-plane location, not a model deployment type.

properties.actionGroup: Required existing approved action-group resource ID; no recipient or subscription invented.
properties.semantics: Count exact Operations success events in the inclusive interval [ago(3m), now()]. A last success older than three minutes, or no success, produces MissingSuccess=1 even for empty input; no grouping or union.
properties.windowSize: PT15M; query scan range, not the three-minute missing-success threshold.
properties.activation: Rule omitted by default. Enabling requires watchdogQueryReadiness evidence: initial AppEvents ingestion/schema, private AAD query access and one-minute query validation. Never fake an Operations success for bootstrap. Rule health and measured ingestion/evaluation/delivery remain acceptance gates.

reasoning.whyChosen: Reliability: missing success must alarm independently of the agent runtime.
reasoning.tradeoffs: No guaranteed three-minute cloud notification latency. Keep the pilot acceptance gate open if measured ingestion/evaluation/delivery misses the profile; do not extend the threshold. The separate five-minute in-app escalation deadline is not a heartbeat tolerance.

properties.lifecycleDeletion: Not configured; class-specific retention needs approval.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security/reliability: versioned evidence, separate quarantine and approved-package boundaries, recoverable accidental deletion.
alternativesConsidered: A single immutable bucket for all data classes
reasoning.tradeoffs: Soft delete/versioning are recovery features, not WORM or an independently protected archive.

properties.limits: 2048 MB candidate, 40-instance per-scaling-group ceiling. Workflows always-ready durable/http, independent Operations function:DeadlineWatchdog; not a quota guarantee or total-spend cap.
properties.operations: Independent SQL deadline/lease/outbox tick every 30 seconds; emits unsampled cohors.watchdog.completed only after successful SQL completion, AppRoleName cohors-operations. No dependency on API, Foundry or Search for the tick.

reasoning.whyChosen: Reliability: independent Operations timer/watchdog and replay-safe Durable Workflow hosts.
reasoning.tradeoffs: No Flex slots. Packages, trigger discovery, App Insights AAD ingestion, private scale access and least-privilege API app roles must be tested.

overallReasoning.summary: Prepare the approved small PaaS architecture with private identity-based data access, SQL authority, reconstructable projections and independently monitored operations. Do not deploy resources or fabricate integration evidence.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: WAF/insights/schema-specific MCP tools are unavailable; current Microsoft Learn pages, official schemas and one consolidated WAF/naming research pass replace them. Naming documentation omits exact managed-environment/model-deployment constraints; conservative generated names plus a live preflight remain necessary. Region/SKU/model/quotas/pricing, landing-zone egress/private access, Entra, image/package publication, runtime integration, strict EU processing boundaries, external protected ledger digests and recovery are open deployment/operations gates. Pilot defaults do not promise HA, RPO/RTO, regulatory compliance or production retention. No AKS, Cosmos DB, additional broker, azd, clinical connection or automatic global failover is introduced.

architecturePrinciples: SQL is the authoritative state, with transactional audit/outbox/inbox.
Human medical and regulatory decisions remain distinct; no workload identity may approve.
Public data-plane access and shared-key authentication are disabled.
EU-bounded processing requires feature/deployment-type review, not a region label alone.
No locked retention or protected-digest assurance without its explicit acceptance gate.
No empty test suite, skipped SQL tests, silent fallback or success-shaped placeholder.
Foundation provisioning and functional cloud readiness are separate.
